## Strongest outcome

**I derived a size-uniform classicalization theorem that extends your qubit programme to arbitrary fixed-dimensional qudits and known, correlated, symmetry-invariant quantum systems.** Combining the interacting-spin version with one specific result from OpenAI’s release gives a further, conditional conclusion: **the full weak-field statistical experiment of a three-dimensional quantum ferromagnet becomes equivalent to one classical observation on a sphere—not merely to a limiting magnetization distribution.**

The reusable mechanism is an operator inequality connecting **symmetry, a bounded error in a generator, and preservation of its entire Gibbs state**. A separate argument gives a necessary-and-sufficient classicalization criterion for bounded quantum exponential families.

These are written theorem candidates with explicit proofs and local computational checks. **The requested breakthrough bar is not yet met:** novelty is unestablished, the release-specific physical application retains an unaudited external dependency, and no practical quantum-simulation advantage has been demonstrated.

**Coverage limitation:** this was selective, family-level screening—not a completed technical ingestion or verification of all 372 families. I closely read one of the ten released reasoning summaries, and did not replay any Lean formalization. No callable Sol subagent facility was available, so this was a single-agent investigation. OpenAI’s announcement itself distinguishes the manuscripts, their available formalizations, and the reasoning summaries; I did not treat inclusion in the release as verification. [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/sharing-ai-progress-in-mathematics/)
